island.quest.title: Borrow the strategy, not the picture
island.quest.tip: Lui often leaves wide blank space and dense ink. Van Gogh uses urgent crossing strokes and complementary colour. The point is how they handle feeling, not copying a whole picture.
island.quest.q: To show pressure with a breath of space, which move is real transfer?
island.quest.a: Paste the whole Starry Night picture, then add a lotus.
island.quest.b: Use urgent strokes for anxiety, then spare space and one bright accent to breathe.
island.quest.c: Copy both artists' biographies and birth years.
island.quest.ok: Well done — you took the problem-solving move, not a surface collage.
island.quest.missA: Try again: pasting the whole picture stays on the surface. Pull out stroke and blank-space strategies.
island.quest.missC: Try again: biography matters less. Look at form and your own transfer.

atlas.card.lingnan.title: Lingnan school
atlas.card.lingnan.tip:
Wet pigment and meeting East and West — see how a damp blend makes a sense of air. Traditional brushwork with Western perspective and light.
Read slowly — the point is the method. You do not have to remember it all at once.
atlas.card.expression.title: Expressionism
atlas.card.expression.tip: Expressionism uses brushwork and colour to show a feeling. Read slowly. You do not have to remember it all at once.
atlas.card.feldman.title: Four Feldman steps
atlas.card.feldman.tip: Describe, analyse, interpret, then judge. One step at a time. Read slowly.

island.line.history: Spot how masters solve visual problems
island.line.research: Tell primary looking from second-hand — shoot, ask, touch, note before pasting web images.
island.line.critique: Upgrade casual talk into clear critique.
island.line.sba: Log real process and honest reflection.
island.mq.research.title: Which set counts as primary evidence?
island.mq.research.context: Strong workbooks use your own looking, a survey you made, site photos, and lived experience. Web images and news alone are usually second-hand.
island.mq.research.q: Which set is closer to primary evidence?
island.mq.research.a: Find ten stress pictures online and fill the page.
island.mq.research.b: Seven days of your own photos, a classmate survey, and site poses you shot.
island.mq.research.c: Ask AI to write an 800-word essay that students are stressed.
island.mq.research.ok: Well done — primary evidence comes from what you did and saw yourself.
island.mq.research.missA: Try again: web images are usually second-hand. Shoot, ask, or note it yourself.
island.mq.research.missC: Try again: an AI essay is not your observation, and it is not the art process.
island.mq.critique.title: Upgrade casual talk into clear critique
island.mq.critique.sub: Dark and messy colours → clear, still readable
island.mq.critique.context: This picture is so dark and black, and the lines are a mess. It feels awful to look at.
island.mq.critique.a: The colours are very gloomy, the painter was messy, and it is scary.
island.mq.critique.b: Low-value, low-chroma cools, urgent crossed strokes, and a tight crop build pressure.
island.mq.critique.c: This is an oil painting with black, deep blue, grey, and many lines.
island.mq.critique.ok: Well done — you named how value, chroma, and stroke carry the feeling.
island.mq.critique.missA: Try again: skip vague messy or scary. Name the visual elements.
island.mq.critique.missC: Try again: that line stays on the surface. Say how the elements build the mood.
island.mq.sba.title: Which reflection sounds real?
island.mq.sba.sub: A failed test and the change
island.mq.sba.context: Write what you tried, how it failed, and what you changed. Empty phrases do not show the work was yours.
island.mq.sba.q: Which paragraph fits a process reflection?
island.mq.sba.a: "This piece grapples with the profound metamorphosis of urban alienation..."
island.mq.sba.b: The oil-pastel sheet fell off white glue (test A). Hot glue held (test C), and deeper shadow on the features increased the pressure.
island.mq.sba.c: I had fun, used acrylic and a board, and hope people like it.
island.mq.sba.ok: Well done — you named the trial, the failure, and the change.
island.mq.sba.missA: Try again: vague phrasing does not prove the process. Rewrite the steps you actually tried.
island.mq.sba.missC: Try again: add how you solved the picture or material problem.
island.mq.exam.title: Shared first, then contrasts
island.mq.exam.sub: Two figure sculptures — practice structure, no paper IDs
island.mq.exam.context: First write what they share (subject, medium), then contrast form, space, tone, and movement. Do not finish one image before the other.
island.mq.exam.a: Spend most of the time on image one, and two lines on image two.
island.mq.exam.b: Shared: both are figure or family sculptures. Contrast: one is rounded with negative space; the other is geometric and pushes forward.
island.mq.exam.c: Only say which one you prefer, with no formal analysis.
island.mq.exam.ok: Well done — shared traits and contrasts are both there.
island.mq.exam.missA: Try again: cross-compare both images. Do not write one out fully first.
island.mq.exam.missC: Try again: a preference needs formal analysis behind it.

lesson.f4u3l3.title: November: Getting to know community art — research
lesson.f4u3l3.subtitle: In class, learn what community art is, with past cases for reference. You do not need to go out and run a project.
lesson.f4u3l3.card.theme.body: A community-art theme comes from a real setting — people, places, habits and objects. Start in the classroom, the canteen, the school gate, the way to school, or a memory, and choose one nearby detail to look at.
lesson.f4u3l3.card.observe.body: Use sketches and notes to look at a nearby detail: a corner of the classroom, a canteen seat, the school gate, the way to school, or a memory. Ask permission before photographing people, and respect privacy.
lesson.f4u3l3.card.interview.body: A short classroom interview can ask a classmate which thing in the classroom, the canteen, the school gate, or the way to school they usually do not notice. Keep the questions short, leave pauses, and note the key sentences.
lesson.f4u3l3.card.insight.body: Take one nearby insight from the classroom, the canteen, the school gate, the way to school, or a memory: a detail you had not noticed before that relates to the community. Write clearly what you see, and why it relates to the place and the people.
lesson.f4u3l3.card.practice.body: This lesson is for recognising community art in class. The visual diary continues each week. Practice starts from a nearby detail, for appreciation and insight. The class does not use a real exam paper.
lesson.f4u3l4.title: November: Getting to know community art — develop and make
lesson.f4u3l4.subtitle: In class, look at past cases, then use a classroom exercise to turn that recognition into making. You do not need to go out and run a project.
lesson.f4u3l4.card.make.body: Use a short classroom trial to turn a nearby insight into a making exercise — paper, a pen, clay, or other classroom materials. Write down which materials and skills you use.
lesson.f4u3l4.card.three.body: Use three sentences for this short trial: the theme, how you made it, and what you want the audience to feel. Check the short criteria, then self-assess or ask a classmate to write one sentence.
lesson.f4u3l4.card.practice.body: This lesson practises ways to develop and make in class, with a short trial and a three-sentence talk. The class does not claim an official public-exam result.
lesson.goal.hint: Observable outcomes this lesson asks you to reach
lesson.f4u3l3.goal.1: You can point out the object and focus of appreciation for 「邂逅！山 川 人」, and write the relationship between the clay and the village, the place, and the people.
lesson.f4u3l3.goal.2: You can write one nearby insight from the classroom, the canteen, the school gate, the way to school, or a memory, with a specific enough detail.
lesson.f4u3l3.goal.3: In these two examples, you can write the related visual elements and organisational principles.
lesson.f4u3l4.goal.1: You can point out the object and focus of appreciation for 深食「喚味：𝑥」, and write about food, place, people, and the 「喚味」 invitation.
lesson.f4u3l4.goal.2: In the classroom, you can use paper, a pen, clay, or other classroom materials for a ten-to-fifteen-minute short trial. Do not upload the work.
lesson.f4u3l4.goal.3: You can use three sentences for this short trial: the theme, how you made it, and what you want the audience to feel. Expression stays open, with no single standard answer.
lesson.goal.open: Expression stays open, with no single standard answer.
criteria.insight.title: Short criteria for a nearby insight
criteria.insight.line: The detail is specific enough; it relates to the community; you write the place or the people you see.
criteria.talk.title: Short criteria for the three-sentence talk
criteria.talk.line: The theme is clear; you say how you made it; you say what you want the audience to feel.
criteria.comment.prompt: One sentence from the teacher, a peer, or yourself:
criteria.comment.placeholder: Write one sentence of feedback here.
criteria.note: This step is in-class formative assessment, not a public exam and not HKEAA. It does not predict a public-exam level.

case.hill.frame: This is a past case for reference, used for appreciation with an object and a focus.
appreciate.heading: Appreciation task
case.hill.appreciate.object: Object of appreciation: ceramics made by participating artist 陳思光 with clay from the village (Chuen Lung clay cups / works in village clay).
case.hill.appreciate.focus: Focus of appreciation: the relationship between the clay and the village, the place, and the people.
case.hill.appreciate.task: Look at the official webpage and brochure, and write how the clay works connect the village and the people. This question is not a background introduction.

case.deepfood.appreciate.focus: Focus of appreciation: food, place, and people, and the “喚味” invitation.
case.deepfood.appreciate.task: The class plays the official overview by default, for classroom playback only. Write how you see food, place, and people being invited into “喚味”.

visual.heading: Visual elements and organisational principles
visual.elements.hill: When looking at the ceramics, you can write about material, texture, form, and colour: the clay surface, the cup shape, the fired colour, and how they contrast with or echo the village setting.
visual.principles.near: When looking at nearby details, you can write about space, repetition, and emphasis: how the classroom corridor, the canteen seating, and the school-gate entrance guide the eye.
visual.elements.flavour: When looking at “喚味：𝑥”, you can write about space, colour, movement, and balance: how food, the site, and people are arranged to invite “喚味”.
visual.trial: A short trial can try material and texture, then use contrast, emphasis, or repetition to organise the nearby details you see.

worksheet.intro: This is a classroom activity paper. It follows this lesson’s three tasks: case appreciation, a nearby insight, and a process trace or a three-sentence talk. It is not homework.
worksheet.sampleNote: The following is a sample. It is not a real student or a real school.
worksheet.noSchool: This activity paper does not show a school name, a school crest, or a teacher’s name.
worksheet.l3.q1: Appreciate the ceramics 陳思光 made with clay from the village (Chuen Lung clay cups / works in village clay). Write the relationship between the clay and the village, the place, and the people. Do not only copy the organiser, the planner, or the date.
worksheet.l3.q2: From the classroom, the canteen, the school gate, the way to school, or a memory, choose one nearby detail and write one insight: what do you see? Why does it relate to the community?
worksheet.l3.q3: Use three sentences to say how this nearby detail connects to the appreciation focus of 「邂逅！山 川 人」.
worksheet.l3.q4: Write one insight. Prompt: first write a detail you saw in the classroom materials, then how it relates to the community.
worksheet.l4.q1: Appreciate 深食「喚味：𝑥」. Write how food, place, people, and the 「喚味」 invitation are presented. For classroom playback only. Do not download, upload, or republish.
worksheet.l4.q2: From the classroom, the canteen, the school gate, the way to school, or a memory, choose one nearby detail and write how it could become the theme of a short classroom trial.
worksheet.l4.q3: Use three sentences for this short trial: the theme, how you made it, and what you want the audience to feel. Then, against the short criteria, write one sentence of self-assessment, or ask a classmate to write one sentence.
trial.title: Short classroom trial
trial.when: Mainly in the classroom session on 26 November, for ten to fifteen minutes.
trial.do: Try once with paper, a pen, clay, or other classroom materials. The product only supports a short trial and talk traces.
trial.trace.label: Process trace
trial.trace.hint: Write which materials you tried, what you changed, and why you changed it that way.
trial.talk.label: Three-sentence talk trace
trial.disclaimer: Technology cannot replace a materials trial. This is only a short trial and talk traces.
trial.noUpload: Do not upload the work, and there is no automatic score.
